newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 31.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- Front-page reports of socialist ethical and cultural progress in central Hunan province and northeastern Jilin province.
- China harvests a record 123.95 million tonnes of grain this summer, and 10.75 million tons more than last year
- People's Liberation Army elevates military skills to meet five principles urged by President Jiang Zemin.
- People's Liberation Army and People's Armed Police have contributed to economic development while completing their military training and mission.
- A total of 9,763 overseas-funded joint ventures have been established in the first half of 1997, with contracted foreign funds valued at $22.934 billion
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- Vice Premier Zhu Rongji urges large- and medium-sized state-owned enterprises to deepen reform and step out of loss-making predicament in three years.
- Xu Guangchun, deputy head of Propaganda Department, says important mission of party newspapers is to propagate the upcoming 15th National Congress of the Communist Party
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Governor Dai Xianglong of People's Bank of Chinacalls for improving efficiency of loans
- By July 28, turnover of A and B shares on Shenzhen Stock Exchange totalled 1,288 billion yuan
MARKET DAILY
- Telephone users increased by 10.941 million households in the first half to total 72.741 million
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- ChinaInfo netowrk to open on August 6 to provide most comprehensive information on China
CHINA DAILY
- Premier Li Peng says China will gradually set up a social security system to meet both socialist market economy demands and national conditions.
- China is expecting progress in current talks in Geneva on entry to World Trade Organisation.
- State Council decides to begin a pilot census in small towns and to tighten census management in rural areas.
